catalogue_requests.reason: the catalogue has no class for switching a light source's emission on (cap.imaging.illumination.v1 sets an intensity in percent and cap.optics.set_power.v1 needs mW and is R2; neither maps the upstream enable())

the catalogue has no class for switching a light source's emission off; this action is also the safe state, and the closest classes (cap.optics.shutter.v1, cap.imaging.illumination.v1) do not map the upstream disable()

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: reviewed_by stays null and nothing ran on a laser. The gate raised no warning and no finding on this run. NOT COVERED: the camera path of the clone (microscope.cameras.picamera:PiCamera) and the other laser classes (microscope.lights.sapphire:SapphireLaser, microscope.lights.deepstar:DeepstarLaser, microscope.lights.obis:ObisLaser); this package models the card's first entry symbol, microscope.lights.cobolt:CoboltLaser, only. NOT COVERED: absolute optical power in mW; the head's maximum power is read from the head at connect (gmlp?, microscope/lights/cobolt.py:64) and is not a text-stated bound, so power is published as a fraction of it inside [0, 1] (microscope/abc.py:1245-1247) and the driver does not verify a wattage. NOT COVERED: any trigger capability; the clone fixes software trigger in bulb mode and its trigger raises IncompatibleStateError (microscope/_utils.py:108-140). NOT COVERED: the serial protocol itself; the fake answers get_is_on/get_status with in-memory placeholders and does not replay recorded device replies, and the hardware backend (native.py) was never run. The upstream simulator (microscope/simulators:SimulatedLightSource) is not used as the fake backend: it implements the LightSource ABC, not the Cobolt serial commands, and a backend entry outside the package is imported by the gate, while the clone is never imported or installed. gate.digest is the digest the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-10-29; reviewed_by stays null): accepted after reviewer edits: risk raised from R1 to R2 (a laser above class 1; a class 3B or 4 head is R3, MHS/spec/04-safety.md), so the hardware backend waits for a human signature; native.py and facts.md now say so. After the registry rebuild refreshed task.json, the reviewer re-ran the gate and wrote its digest above.
